transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan M., Priya R., Theo A. (Redwood) — Mark L., Sarah O., Brian C., Jessica K. (Acme Finance)

Summary: quick console tour focusing on per-route cost breakdown, how usage analytics map back to routes and models, and what a pilot would look like.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Mark: Hi Mark Liu, Head of ML at Acme, we'll mostly be evaluating latency and cost impact on our fraud models.
[00:14] Sarah: Sarah, platform eng, I'll be doing the integration.
[00:18] Brian: Brian from finance, here to understand cost.
[00:22] Jessica: Jessica, security. We'll have some questions later about audit logs and KMS.
[00:28] Jordan: Great. Priya will do most of the console walkthrough, I'll chime in on pricing and contracts.
[00:35] Priya: Cool, starting the console — sorry if the screen is a bit slow. Opening the Usage Analytics page. You can see a token breakdown by route, model, and time window.
[00:44] Priya: (shows chart) This per-route chart maps traffic to your API routes. So for you, the fraud-scorer route would show both latency and cost per 1k tokens. We also surface peak concurrency and tail latency percentiles.
[01:05] Sarah: Quick question, how do you attribute tokens to customer routes? We have a single endpoint and route tags internally.
[01:12] Priya: Good call. You can pass route metadata in the call header, or we auto-infer from path. We'll show how that maps in the route settings.
[01:20] Theo: And you can group routes into buckets, e.g., fraud-scorer, enrichment, customer-support, which lets you see cost allocation by business unit.
[01:34] Mark: Nice. On the cost side, how granular is the breakdown? We need to show chargebacks to engineering teams.
[01:40] Priya: We do per-route cost-estimates broken into token compute, embedding units, and model variant multipliers. There's also a cost-explorer where you can filter by model, time, and environment (hosted vs dedicated).
[01:53] Brian: Are these actual invoice numbers or estimates? Accuracy?
[01:56] Jordan: They're estimates tied to your contract rates; for Hosted API it's straightforward per-token. For Dedicated it's based on committed capacity and utilization assumptions — the console shows effective per-token cost under current utilization.
[02:10] Priya: Example: if your quiet hours reduce utilization, Dedicated per-token goes up; console surfaces that so finance can see utilization sensitivity.
[02:20] Mark: That will be important for us, because our fraud-scorer has bursty traffic at market open.
[02:27] Priya: We also have a latency-cost tradeoff widget. You can pin SLOs and get recommendations: batching window, cache TTL for prefixes, or quantized model variants.
[02:39] Mark: Can you show the Optimize suggestions?
[02:42] Priya: Sure — open Optimize -> Recommendations. Here we suggest enabling continuous batching with a 20ms max-wait to reduce per-token CPU, or enabling prefix KV cache for the enrichment route which saves ~30% tokens in our estimate.
[02:56] Sarah: Is KV cache transparent to the app? Any consistency concerns?
[03:01] Priya: It's per-user prefix cache, TTL-based. For deterministic outputs like embeddings it's safe; for transient stateful prompts we recommend shorter TTLs. Also note some transcriptions spelled KV as 'K-V' in older docs, so ignore that.
[03:14] Mark: What about model variants? Can we automatically fall back to cheaper quantized variants during congestion?
[03:20] Theo: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to compatible variants in the same family. The console shows simulated latency and quality delta estimates when you create a rollout policy.
[03:33] Jessica: From security side: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS. Do you surface who called what route? Is there token-level audit logging?
[03:42] Priya: We capture request-level metadata for audit; audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM. KMS integration available for private deployments and Dedicated — you can use your own keys for model payload encryption.
[03:55] Jessica: Is Redwood SOC two?
[03:58] Jordan: We are SOC 2 Type II certified — apologies the packet is 'SOC two' in one of our older slides, typo. We'll send the compliance packet after the call.
[04:08] Mark: Can you demonstrate a per-route drilldown?
[04:12] Priya: Yep clicking into fraud-scorer route — here are slow requests, top input sizes, and the model variants used. We also surface token distribution histogram which helps identify if prompts are large and if batching will help.
[04:29] Sarah: For integration how do we pass route tags and metadata? We use Kong API gateway currently.
[04:35] Priya: We have header-based tagging and SDK helpers. For Kong you can map request path to route header at the gateway layer.
[04:43] Brian: Finance question: what's the example delta between Hosted per-token vs Dedicated at 70% utilization?
[04:49] Jordan: Rough ballpark: Hosted for our curated open models might be $0.XX per 1k tokens; Dedicated with committed GPUs at 70% utilization could get to 40-60% of hosted cost depending on model/quantization. We'll send a model-by-model pricing sheet.
[05:05] Mark: Any gotchas on cold starts or KV cache priming?
[05:10] Priya: Cold KV priming shows as higher costs early in the window; console flags cold start events and suggests prewarm windows. Also note that very short sequences can change kernel selection which affects latency, but console shows kernel-level perf for the detailed technical deep-dive view.
[05:31] Mark: We have compliance constraints — some data must stay in our VPC. Is Private deployment mandatory?
[05:36] Jordan: If data residency/VPC is required, our Private deployment supports customer-managed networking or on-prem packaging. Dedicated can be VPC peered and provide strong isolation. We'll include the VPC architecture doc.
[05:49] Jessica: How about encryption at rest and in transit?
[05:52] Priya: TLS for transit, and optional KMS for at-rest keys. For Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS.
[06:00] Sarah: Can the console surface per-route SLA breaches?
[06:03] Theo: Yep alerts and SLO widgets. You can set per-route targets and get automatic rollback to a more robust variant or route traffic to a fallback region if latency spikes.
[06:16] Mark: Speaking of regions, do you support multi-region fallbacks with routing?
[06:19] Priya: Smart routing supports region-based policies, and the console simulates cross-region latency impact in the routing planner.
[06:27] Brian: For finance, we need a forecast that maps predicted traffic to monthly bill and to Dedicated commit sizing.
[06:33] Jordan: The console Forecast tab exports a CSV with utilization assumptions and estimated monthly cost. We'll run a sample forecast for your 7-day traffic after you share it.
[06:44] Mark: Great. Can we look at a sample pivot: route-level chargeback for last 30 days?
[06:49] Priya: (loads pivot) Here's the table: fraud-scorer 48% of token cost, enrichment 28%, support 12%, other 12%. You can export and map to cost centers.
[07:04] Sarah: Is there an API to pull these metrics programmatically?
[07:08] Theo: Yes there's a metrics API and a streaming webhook for live alerts.
[07:14] Jessica: About audit logs — how long retained? Does Redwood keep PII in logs?
[07:20] Jordan: Retention configurable; for Hosted we keep request metadata but not full payloads by default unless you opt-in for debug logs. For Dedicated/Private you control log retention and can route logs off to your storage.
[07:35] Mark: We also use embeddings heavily; does the console split embedding cost separately?
[07:40] Priya: Yes embeddings are a separate unit in the cost model and show up as their own line items in the cost breakdown.
[07:48] Brian: Any examples of optimization that reduced monthly bill?
[07:51] Priya: A customer we worked with moved enrichment to cached prompts and a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical traffic — they saw ~45% reduction in embedding compute cost.
[08:02] Mark: Can you simulate what happens if we enable batching with a 50ms window? I'm worried about latency impact on fraud decisions.
[08:09] Priya: In the policy simulator you can set latency SLOs and it will show the expected tradeoff. For fraud-scorer we often recommend micro-batching at 10-30ms to preserve p99.
[08:20] Sarah: Is there an SDK or middleware to do client-side fallback?
[08:24] Theo: We have language SDKs with built-in retry and fallback hooks, and sample middleware for node/java to do client-side degrade to smaller models.
[08:34] Mark: Security follow-up — Jessica will need encryption details and evidence of SOC2 controls.
[08:38] Jessica: Also RBAC: can we restrict access to cost dashboards to finance only?
[08:42] Priya: Yes RBAC is fine-grained; you can restrict routes, dashboards, and even datasets.
[08:48] Jordan: Wrapping up, do you feel this answers the main questions for a pilot?
[08:52] Mark: Yes, next step is to get the pricing and the benchmark template. We'll share our 7-day traffic and pick a pilot route (fraud-scorer).
[09:00] Brian: And I'll evaluate the cost forecast with finance.
[09:03] Jessica: I'll follow up on compliance items.
[09:07] Jordan: Great. We'll send the deck and pricing. Estimated pilot timeline if everything looks good — 4 weeks to pilot start.

Notes / Imperfections: occasional transcription errors (Redwood Consol vs Console, SOC two typo), speaker labels generic at times.

Action recap: Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated options; Priya to run benchmarks; Mark to send traffic profiles; Jessica to request SOC2 packet.
